articles.title: Navalia: Advancing Cowork Agents through Verifiable Task Synthesis and Long-Horizon Post-Training
articles.summary: Large language model (LLM) agents are evolving from conversational assistants into Cowork Agents capable of autonomous planning, tool use, and complex task execution.
articles.paragraph: Large language model (LLM) agents are evolving from conversational assistants into Cowork Agents capable of autonomous planning, tool use, and complex task execution. Financial analysis requires these agents to integrate cross-document evidence and perform multistep numerical reasoning, but expert task authoring is costly, while direct LLM synthesis struggles to produce challenging tasks with reliable answers. We introduce Navalia, a framework for Cowork Agents that combines verifiable task synthesis with long-horizon post-training.

articles.title: DataPraxis: Scaling Analytics Tasks via Verified Workspace Evolution
articles.summary: General-purpose agents are increasingly expected to perform professional analytics work, which requires sustained reasoning, iterative investigation, and reliable evidence.
articles.paragraph: General-purpose agents are increasingly expected to perform professional analytics work, which requires sustained reasoning, iterative investigation, and reliable evidence. Training these capabilities requires diverse and challenging tasks. However, generating tasks directly from raw data often overlooks deeper questions that emerge through analysis and provides limited evidence for verification. To address these limitations, we introduce DataPraxis, an analytics task synthesis framework based on verified workspace evolution. The framework progressively enriches workspaces with validated findings and artifacts, then inherits and combines these workspaces to uncover deeper questions.

articles.title: Fix, Not Just Resample: Bounded Compiler-Guided Repair in Lean 4
articles.summary: Automated theorem provers often rely on sampling language models, but proof assistants like Lean reject each failed step with a precise error message --- information that pure sampling discards.
articles.paragraph: Automated theorem provers often rely on sampling language models, but proof assistants like Lean reject each failed step with a precise error message --- information that pure sampling discards. To overcome this, we introduce a bounded, online step-level repair module. Our search samples $K$ candidate tactics at each step and repairs a failed tactic at most $R$ times. Instead of discarding failed tactics, we feed the compiler's error message to a pretrained repair model to fix individual rejected steps in place. This approach improves the solve rate over a sampling-only baseline across all tested candidate budgets ($K \in \{1,3,5,8\}$), achieving up to a $32\%$ relative gain and solving $82$ additional theorems on a $1{,}990$-theorem subset of the LeanDojo benchmark.

articles.title: When Planning Problems Become Hard for LLMs: Separating Structural Complexity from Semantic Interpretability
articles.summary: Large language models (LLMs) struggle with classical planning, but benchmarks rarely distinguish structural difficulty from the difficulty of interpreting symbolic vocabulary.
articles.paragraph: Large language models (LLMs) struggle with classical planning, but benchmarks rarely distinguish structural difficulty from the difficulty of interpreting symbolic vocabulary. We examine seven STRIPS domains with BFS-optimal plan lengths. For predicting structural difficulty without solving an instance, the zero-training delete-relaxation heuristic $h_{\mathrm{add}}$ outperforms learned alternatives on held-out domains (mean Spearman $|\rho|=0.931$), including ridge regression ($0.707$), object count ($0.657$), and the episodic retrieval architecture ARC ($0.400$). ARC also fails to outperform a linear model using the same features. To isolate semantic effects, we progressively rename predicates while preserving states, transitions, and optimal plans.

articles.title: Bring new talent and expertise into your company with InnoNext
articles.summary: EIC-supported companies can host talented researchers and innovators for up to six months, fully funded.
articles.paragraph: EIC-supported companies can host talented researchers and innovators for up to six months, fully funded. Looking to access new expertise or bring a fresh perspective to your company? EIC-supported companies can host talented researchers and innovators through the Next Generation Innovation Talents’ Initiative InnoNext - with placements of 3 to 6 months fully funded. The model is already delivering results: 415 matches between companies and talents have been validated, with 112 internships already activated and 226 opportunities currently open for talented researchers and innovators. Hosting an InnoNext talent gives companies the opportunity to bring highly skilled researchers and innovators into their teams, adding knowledge, perspectives and technical expertise to ongoing projects.

articles.title: Nurses’ perceptions of an audiovisual material to support patient education on oral health management in diabetes care
articles.summary: by Rie Kudoh, Taiga Shibayama Educational support for nurses is essential to promote oral health management education for patients with diabetes.
articles.paragraph: by Rie Kudoh, Taiga Shibayama Educational support for nurses is essential to promote oral health management education for patients with diabetes. However, few studies have focused on supporting nurses in this context. This study explored the effects of an audiovisual material designed to support nurses’ patient education on oral health management in diabetes care. Semi-structured interviews were conducted with eight certified diabetes nurse educators. Data were analyzed using content analysis.

articles.title: Cognitive effects of untreated unilateral and bilateral hearing loss in midlife: Preliminary evidence
articles.summary: by Lakshmi Satheesan, Usha Shastri, Gagan Bajaj, Mohan Kumar Kalaiah Hearing loss has been identified as a modifiable risk factor for cognitive decline and dementia, although most of the evidence is d...
articles.paragraph: by Lakshmi Satheesan, Usha Shastri, Gagan Bajaj, Mohan Kumar Kalaiah Hearing loss has been identified as a modifiable risk factor for cognitive decline and dementia, although most of the evidence is derived from studies in older adults. Identifying such cognitive impairment in midlife is crucial, as it serves as a baseline for understanding changes in cognitive abilities that occur later in life. The present study aimed to compare the cognitive performance of age- and socioeconomic status-matched middle-aged adults with normal hearing and those with untreated hearing loss. This study included 48 participants aged 40–65 years, comprising 24 adults with normal hearing and 24 with untreated hearing loss. Among the latter participants, 9 had unilateral loss and 15 had bilateral loss.

articles.title: Bitcoin Optech Newsletter #427
articles.summary: This week’s newsletter summarizes the disclosure of two denial-of-service vulnerabilities in older versions of Eclair and describes a proposed scheme for running complex multi-round contracts inside L...
articles.paragraph: ● Disclosure of two DoS vulnerabilities fixed in Eclair v0.14.1: Erick Cestari posted to Delving Bitcoin the responsible disclosure of two denial-of-service (DoS) vulnerabilities in the channel opening process of Eclair v0.14.0 and earlier. Both were fixed in Eclair #3324 and released in v0.14.1 in July, and users running an older version should upgrade. The first, found by Matt Morehouse with his smite fuzzer, is a race condition in a duplicate temporary_channel_id check. Eclair checked whether the ID was already in use before accepting an open_channel message, but did not record the new channel until a later step, so an attacker sending several identical open_channel messages in quick succession could get two past the check.
